subject: Re: Renewal discussion — Rate guard + short-term burst capacity
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@acme.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: Priya Desai <priya@acme.com>
Date: Sun, 7 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal negotiation + short-term uplift needs

Jonas — thanks for the call last week. As we approach our renewal window we want to: (1) increase committed capacity by ~20% to cover a planned product launch in Q2, and (2) get a short-term guarantee on pricing while we validate traffic patterns (we need predictability for internal finance).

Attached is a snapshot of our last 3 months of usage to help the sizing. Our procurement team will push for a price hold or a predictable step-up rather than a floating usage tier. If Redwood can offer a temporary price guarantee and a modest bridging credit for the burst, we can commit to the increased monthly baseline for 12 months.

Questions:
- Can you provide a 60–90 day price guard on current units?
- Any standard bridging/burst credit mechanics you use (credits that amortize against overage charges)?
- Will a 20% uplift to committed units be eligible for the same discounted rate?

Thanks — looking to move quickly.

Sanjay Rao
Head of ML Platforms
ACME Corp
[attachment: ACME_Q1_usage.csv (csv)]

From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@acme.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 7 Feb 2027 11:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal negotiation + short-term uplift needs

Sanjay — appreciate the context and the file. We have a proposal that should match what you described and keep both sides protected while you validate the launch. High level:

- Rate Guard ("RateGuard"): a 75-day price guarantee on current per-unit rates for baseline and the uplifted committed units. During the guard window, your effective billed rate will not increase even if list pricing changes.
- Burst Credit: a one-time pool of 200k token credits to cover burst traffic for the launch window (applies to overages across host/dedicated). Credits are consumed first, then normal billing applies.
- Commit adjustment: a 20% uplift to the committed baseline for 12 months; we’ll do a single true-up at month 6 and final true-up at renewal.
- Eligibility: uplifted commit inherits the same volume discount band that applies to the baseline.

If these items look fine I can send the small amendment (RateGuard_TOS_v1.pdf) that captures the guard window lengths, credit expiry (90 days from execution), and the true-up cadence. There are two optional clauses to consider: a usage-smoothing clause (reduces true-up volatility over the first 3 months) and a limited SLA credit in case of sustained latency degradation around the launch.

Notes for transparency: this offer assumes no change to our data residency/Security scope and is contingent on the signed amendment and the new commit schedule.

Jonas Weber
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Office: +1 415-555-0123

Team — forwarding Jonas' reply and the attached draft TOS. I ran the numbers against ACME's usage and the proposed 20% uplift. Quick summary of the commercial impact (high level):

- Baseline uplift (20%): increases ARR vs current commit by ~22% given volume bands; margin stays healthy with existing discount tiering.
- Burst credit (200k tokens): modeled as contra-revenue over the first quarter; net impact to Q1 bookings ~-3.1% but unlocks the 12-month commit uplift.
- RateGuard (75 days): limited-term exposure; if list prices rise during the guard we hold their effective unit price — largest risk is if their usage spikes beyond the new committed baseline before credits are consumed.

Recommended approval: accept RateGuard + 200k burst credit + 12-month 20% uplift with the following internal guardrails:
1) Credit expiry 90 days from execution, non-negotiable.
2) Usage smoothing clause enabled (averaging across months 1–3 for true-up) to avoid one-off spikes.
3) Exec sign-off from revenue ops on final amendment before DocuSign.

Aditya — can you confirm the legal/finance redlines for the RateGuard_TOS_v1.pdf? Neha — any flags on SLA credit language?

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Head of Sales Strategy | Redwood Inference
